review.method: Agent inspected the extracted checkpoint text and physical-page manifest; maintainer review pending. No automatic relevance scorer was used; source inspection and labels were authored by the agent.
review.scope: Curated sufficient evidence pages, not an exhaustive relevance judgment of all 883 pages.
review.prior_cases: Preserves five Phase 1 questions. Broad scope is answerable from the book, even when retrieved title-only evidence is insufficient. Follow-up history is frozen for reproducible comparisons.

expected_claims.claim: An interpreter traverses a source program represented as a data structure and simulates it by calling primitive subroutines.
Interpretation organizes execution in source-language abstractions and supports interactive development and debugging.

history.content: An interpreter executes source programs by analyzing them and calling primitive procedures.

expected_claims.claim: The Scheme interpreter evaluates an entered number such as 486 and displays the same number.
The nearby discussion shows arithmetic combinations and nested expressions evaluated by the interpreter.
Page 1 gives the SICP title, second-edition note, Harold Abelson and Gerald Jay Sussman with Julie Sussman, and Alan J. Perlis foreword credit.
The parsed title page has an omitted image marker.
The book teaches techniques for controlling complexity in software through abstraction, conventional interfaces, and languages.
It uses a Lisp dialect to develop procedural and data abstractions and modular decomposition.
It develops mechanisms for combining and abstracting procedures and data.

cases.question: What was the weather in Kolkata yesterday?

expected_claims.claim: State that the indexed SICP material does not provide enough evidence for the weather; do not invent weather facts.

cases.question: How does an evaluator carry out a source-language program by invoking primitives on a machine?

expected_claims.claim: The interpreter analyzes a source-program data structure and invokes primitive subroutines implemented in the native language.
It organizes execution in the abstractions of the source language.

cases.question: Across physical PDF pages 37-39, how does the discussion move from nested expressions to naming values and the environment?

expected_claims.claim: Nested prefix combinations can contain other combinations.
The read-eval-print loop reads, evaluates, and prints; define associates a value with a name such as size.
The environment is the memory that tracks name-object pairs and supports incremental program construction.

cases.question: Compare the roles of procedure abstraction in Chapter 1 and compound-data abstraction at the start of Chapter 2.

expected_claims.claim: Chapter 1 combines primitive operations into compound procedures and uses define and higher-order procedures for abstraction.
Chapter 2 combines primitive data into compound objects to raise the conceptual level, modularity, and expressive power of programs.
